summary.headline: Shanti Gold's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 73.4% YoY to INR746 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to about 5.7% as management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR3,200-3,500 crores.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 73.4% YoY to INR746 crores in Q2 FY27 and 102.3% to INR1,462.3 crores in H1, with volumes up 25.4% in the quarter to 535.5 kgs and 41% in H1 to 1,057.6 kgs. Q2 EBITDA rose 15.6% to INR42.5 crores and PAT rose 13.5% to INR29.6 crores, but EBITDA growth lagged revenue sharply and margin fell. Management attributed this to the Marol facility ramp-up, new product verticals and the upcoming Jaipur plant, calling the moderation transitional, and guided EBITDA margin to 5-7%. The company raised about INR99.83 crores via rights issue, which management said has been fully deployed into working capital.

financial_highlights.change: +73.4% YoY vs INR430 crores in Q2 FY26
Share of revenue reported as 6% vs 4% earlier; roughly doubled

segments.name: Domestic B2B manufacturing (retail chains and jewellery players)
segments.commentary: Volume growth driven by retail partners; company is expanding into North and East India beyond South and West. Product mix now includes designer, Turkish and plain/CZ/advanced categories.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue reported at INR82 crores, with share rising from 4% to 6%; management guides 6-7% for FY27. Dubai office approvals in place, with volumes expected once market settles.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reiterated at INR3,200-3,500 crores (about 60% growth over FY26); CFO later said likely INR3,100-3,200 crores plus, while stating he would not give an exact number.
Volume growth guidance of roughly 25-30% for the year; historical volume CAGR cited at about 43-44%.
EBITDA margin guided at 5-7% on a sustainable basis, down from earlier commentary; product mix cited as the reason for the revision.
Jaipur facility (about 65,000 sq ft built on 3 acres) now expected to start around January or February 2027 after interior and electrical work, delayed from earlier November guidance.
Management expects utilisation of 75-80% of manufacturing capacity once Jaipur and other facilities are operational.
Debt-equity: currently about 0.5x; company is comfortable up to 1x. GML (gold metal loans) at 15-20% of stock, with comfort up to 30%.
capex_capacity: Marol extended manufacturing facility commenced operations in H1 FY27, adding capacity and flexibility; management says it enabled volume growth of 41% in H1.
Jaipur facility: building of about 65,000 sq ft (expanded from 50,000 sq ft) on 3 acres, to make machine-made plain gold jewellery; interior and electrical work ongoing, start targeted Jan-Feb 2027.
Company referred to a 1,200 kg-capacity facility and said it can scale to tonnes annually; management said the Jaipur plant will be funded from internal resources without fresh debt.
New jewellery lines launched in the last three months (including handmade chains) are reportedly only 10-15% operational.
demand_pricing: Management says demand from retail partners is healthy into Dhanteras, Diwali and the wedding season; it remains optimistic for H2.
Average gold inventory holding cost cited at about INR13,500 per gram; management says it does not target inventory gains.
Gold price reference: about INR1,50,000 per 10 grams at the time of guidance, now about INR1,40,000 per 10 grams per management.
Management says it is facing no order issues from recent gold price moves, citing in-house designers rolling out new designs.
Competitive positioning: company describes itself as one of the leading organised gold manufacturers, with a focus on market share over short-term margin; no direct competitor pricing data given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin decline, and is the 5-7% range sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin moderation to a growth and investment phase, upfront costs of new verticals and facilities, and product mix; it called the moderation transitional and guided 5-7% EBITDA margin as sustainable near term.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt can the company carry and how is working capital being funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Current debt-equity is about 0.5x, with the company comfortable up to 1x; working capital is being funded through a mix of debt and equity, and advance gold is being considered as a future vertical.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY27 guidance of INR3,200-3,500 crores still achievable given Jaipur delay and gold price falls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the range and said it is confident of being within it, while the CFO said the figure is likely INR3,100-3,200 crores plus; the chairman said gold at INR1,40,000 per 10 grams is still consistent with the range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the rights issue proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: The entire INR98-99.83 crore rights issue proceeds have been used for working capital, per the chairman.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR18 crores invested in Ratnaveer Precision and Lalithaa Jewellery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described it as a one-off treasury deployment for short-term returns, with liquid holdings, not a strategic diversification.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Utssav and Shanti Gold not merged, and do they overlap?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said the two are run by different managements, do not overlap customers or product lines, and that a merger is not ruled out but not decided.

risks_watch: EBITDA margin fell to about 5.7% in Q2 with PAT margin near 4%; management has not given a timeline for recovery beyond 'as scale comes in'.
Jaipur facility delayed from November to January-February 2027, affecting H2 volume and the FY27 guidance.
Working capital intensity and inventory build-up: management expects inventory to stay elevated for a couple of quarters; funding mix between debt and equity still open.
Gold price correction (reported 6-7% fall in the past month) could affect Q3 margins; the company says it relies on natural hedging and only uses GML at 15-20% of stock.
Revenue guidance wording shifted from INR3,200-3,500 crores to a CFO comment of INR3,100-3,200 crores plus; watch Q3 for clarity.
Related-party exposure and governance: investments in Ratnaveer Precision and Lalithaa Jewellery, and the parallel Utssav group company, with merger undecided.
Export and Dubai office contribution remains small and delayed by market conditions.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and long-term scale, but defensive and evasive on margins, guidance quantum and debt plans. Management repeatedly deflected specific numbers as forward-looking and framed the margin drop as transitional.
key_quotes: So, our strategy remains very simple, to focus on gaining market share rather than optimizing for short-term margins.
And we are quite bullish in this segment.

We are giving very cautious guidance of 5 to 7% because there are many levers in the play regarding the product mix, the kind of design that we are rolling out, the kind of market we are in, the kind of price mechanism that is being played out.
So we see the current margin moderation as transitional rather than structural.

adds.what: Jaipur plant, ~65,000 sq ft building on 3 acres (machine-made plain gold jewellery), funded internally

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR3,200-3,500 crores (about 60% growth), backed by the commissioned Marol facility, H1 volume growth of 41% and healthy retail demand, but no firm order book is cited; the Jaipur plant slipped to Jan-Feb 2027 and the EBITDA margin guide was cut to 5-7%, while the CFO later hinted at a lower INR3,100-3,200 crore range.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin compressed to about 5.7% (EBITDA INR42.5 cr on INR746 cr revenue) and management guided a 5-7% range, with no concrete recovery timeline beyond 'as scale comes in'.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Jaipur plant (about 65,000 sq ft on 3 acres) slipped from November to January-February 2027, and the Marol extension is already commissioned, so the next addition lands in Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 volume grew 41% to 1,057.6 kgs and Q2 grew 25.4% to 535.5 kgs; guidance is 25-30% for the year, with retail demand healthy into Diwali and weddings.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not disclosed, and management only says it expects 75-80% once Jaipur and other facilities run; the Jaipur build is already committed and funded internally, so a new announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR3,200-3,500 cr was held, but the CFO said INR3,100-3,200 cr plus, and the Jaipur delay and 6-7% gold price fall weigh on H2.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: The CFO's INR3,100-3,200 cr comment sits below the INR3,200-3,500 cr range, the Jaipur plant slipped, and the EBITDA margin guide was cut to 5-7%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New jewellery lines (including handmade chains) launched in the last three months are only 10-15% operational, and advance gold is being considered as a future vertical.

rows.label: Export ramp via Dubai office
rows.why: Exports reached INR82 cr and share rose from 4% to 6% (guided 6-7% for FY27), but volumes are expected only once the market settles.

rows.label: Inventory build and rights-issue deployment
rows.why: The full INR98-99.83 cr rights issue went into working capital, and management expects inventory to stay elevated for a couple of quarters, with debt-equity at 0.5x against a 1x comfort level.

rows.label: Possible Utssav-Shanti Gold merger
rows.why: The chairman said a merger is not ruled out but not decided, and the two groups have separate managements with no customer or product overlap.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, Marol commissioning and the INR3,200-3,500 cr revenue range, but cautious and evasive on margin recovery, the CFO's lower revenue comment, and related-party investments; analysts pushed on margin sustainability, guidance quantum and the Jaipur delay.
